key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence can non-destructively distinguish interface- versus bulk-dominated degradation in perovskite solar cells, revealing that PEABF4 initially passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but later accelerates deeper degradation under heat.
engineering_relevance: This provides a depth-sensitive diagnostic for tracking stability losses in perovskite stacks, helping engineers target interface treatments and aging pathways more effectively.
method: Multiwavelength excitation PL to probe different absorption depths
Compare PL decay signatures before and after thermal aging
Use diffusion-recombination simulations to link signals to surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime
evidence_signal: The abstract reports excitation-wavelength-dependent PL decay changes that match simulated behavior, showing interfacial recombination reduction after PEABF4 treatment and broader recombination losses after thermal aging.
watch_item: PL interpretation depends on modeling assumptions and may not uniquely separate all interfacial and bulk mechanisms without complementary measurements.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
